journey.currentState: Shop checkout and trainer/group transfers are atomic, revision-checked, realtime-published operations.

gaps.detail: Items acquired outside checkout or transfer are entered through editable inventory rows.
Trainer rows may omit stable row IDs and store only display names.

journey.currentState: Group rows have stable IDs. Stack transfer is atomic, but target merging still uses normalized display-name identity.

gaps.detail: Canonical identity, serialized item state, reservations, and provenance are not stored on every row.
General inventory save accepts direct setup edits outside an operation receipt.

journey.currentState: Trainer slots and a Pokémon held-item string exist, with a small set of name-resolved derived bonuses.

gaps.detail: Equipping edits descriptive strings and does not atomically move a stable inventory instance.
Only selected held-item effects are hard-coded; source loss and stale offers are not uniformly reconciled.

journey.currentState: The generic presentation contract exposes inventory affordances, but ordinary items are not executable offers. HP, conditions, stages, resources, replay, and realtime authorities already exist independently.

gaps.detail: Inventory affordances have no linked item offer and declaration only authorizes the offer rather than applying item mechanics.
Users currently consume an item and apply HP, condition, stage, or action changes through separate commands or sheet edits.
No one operation currently binds source row, action cost, target effects, history, and exact replay.

journey.currentState: Encounter lifecycle, objectives, clocks, phases, accepted history, capture, and sheet mutation exist as separate authorities.

gaps.detail: Completing lifecycle does not create a versioned consequence/reward settlement document.
XP, loot, captures, cleanup, and objective outcomes are settled through separate screens or commands.

journey.currentState: Campaign-day recovery and breeding attention exist, while advancement and unresolved campaign work remain distributed across sheets.

gaps.detail: Level, move, evolution, treatment, team overflow, capture, hatch, and ownership decisions do not share an attention-item authority.
Campaign page offers only the irreversible next-day action and no role-projected continuation dashboard.
